items.item: volumeClaimTemplates provides stable, per-Pod storage
persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy's whenDeleted and whenScaled policies, each Delete or Retain
Strimzi used workarounds for StatefulSet limitations such as asymmetric storage configuration
Pods managed by a single StatefulSet always exist only on a single Kubernetes cluster
StrimziPodSet is used internally by the Cluster Operator; users must not create, update, or delete it
a KRaft-mode Kafka cluster requires Kafka and KafkaNodePool custom resources
rack.topologyKey (e.g. topology.kubernetes.io/zone) enables rack-aware broker assignment to improve fault tolerance, within one location
deleteClaim controls whether a node pool's PVCs are deleted automatically
support for ZooKeeper-based Apache Kafka clusters and for KRaft migration has been removed
clusters must already be using KRaft before upgrading
rolling should happen without impacting any topic's min.isr
determines whether a broker can be rolled without affecting acks=all producers on topics with min.insync.replicas set
the logged decision when a roll would remove a broker from the ISR, stalling acks=all producers

sources.source: Apache Flink Kubernetes Operator documentation, Job Management

items.item: three supported upgrade modes: stateless, last-state, savepoint
savepoint mode provides maximal safety and the possibility to serve as a backup or fork point; needs a running job, falls back to the last checkpoint if unhealthy
last-state mode works in any application state and does not require a healthy job

sources.source: Apache Flink Kubernetes Operator documentation, Autoscaler

items.item: the operator's built-in autoscaler adjusts parallelism per vertex based on observed load, not per job

sources.source: Apache Flink documentation, Checkpoints vs. Savepoints

items.item: a checkpoint's lifecycle is managed by Flink: created, owned, and released without user interaction, deleted automatically unless configured otherwise
a savepoint is created, owned and deleted solely by the user; Flink never deletes it
FileSystemCheckpointStorage is configured with a filesystem URL and persists checkpoint snapshots there
EmbeddedRocksDBStateBackend holds in-flight data on the TaskManager's local data directories by default

the native Kubernetes persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy field applies to StatefulSet-managed Pods specifically; a Strimzi-managed Kafka cluster's brokers run under StrimziPodSet, not a native StatefulSet, so Strimzi's own deleteClaim field — not the native retention policy — is the mechanism that actually governs broker PVC deletion in practice

KafkaAvailability's check is per-partition: a broker hosting many topics is blocked from rolling if removing it would hurt even one of them, regardless of how safe the others are — the same all-or-nothing logic examples.py models directly

a PodDisruptionBudget alone does not know about Kafka's ISR; it only limits how many Pods matching its selector can be unavailable at once. The actual ISR-awareness comes from KafkaAvailability inside the operator refusing its own roll — the PDB and Drain Cleaner together redirect an external eviction into that same operator-owned check, rather than the PDB itself understanding replication

at.step: Drain Cleaner and the budget's half

items.item: last-state upgrade mode's reliance on 'the latest checkpoint information' means its safety is only as good as how recently a checkpoint was actually taken — the operator's own max-allowed-checkpoint-age setting exists specifically because a stale checkpoint under last-state can silently fall back to savepoint behavior instead

the relationship between Kafka's KRaft controller quorum and general consensus theory (Raft/Paxos) is real but this topic does not teach the quorum algorithm itself — it is declared knowledge here, the same way de.linearizability declares it, because no Data Engineering topic introduces it yet

at.out: a declared cross-chapter gap; see OUTLINE.md

items.item: object storage for Flink checkpoints and local disk for RocksDB's live state are not interchangeable roles even though both involve the word 'state': swapping them (trying to run RocksDB directly on object storage, or treating the checkpoint directory as the only copy needed for low-latency access) defeats the reason each exists

a StrimziPodSet depends on the Strimzi operator itself to recreate a deleted Pod, unlike a native StatefulSet where the Kubernetes controller manager does that recreation on its own — a Strimzi deployment running with only one operator replica therefore has a single point of failure for that specific recovery path that a plain StatefulSet-based workload wouldn't have

rack awareness as Strimzi configures it is explicitly scoped to a single location (the doc's own words: 'not across regions') — it spreads replicas across zones within one region's worth of latency, not across geographically separate regions, which would need a different design entirely

stateless upgrade mode discards all state by design and is explicitly not the mode a production stateful job should use for a routine upgrade — its presence in the three-mode list is for the case where starting over really is acceptable, not a shortcut around the other two

the Flink autoscaler's metrics-only mode (observe and recommend without acting) is the documented way to build confidence in its recommendations before letting it actually resize a production job — skipping straight to live scaling is a choice the docs themselves steer away from
